# Idea: "Animaciones" tab with Manim videos generated by the tutor agent

**Status:** idea only, nothing built. Written down on 2026-10-18 so it can be picked up later.
**Verdict:** feasible, about a day for a working MVP. The risky parts are running generated code safely and the install weight, not the idea.

## What it is
The classroom gets a new tab, **Animaciones**. When it makes sense while teaching, the voice tutor asks for a short Manim animation of a concept. Generation takes a while, so the tutor keeps talking about something else. When the video is ready it appears in the tab and the tutor is told, so it can comment on it.

## Why it fits the current code
- The agent (`agents/aulaquipu-tutor/src/agent.ts`) already uses `tool()` calls that publish to data-channel topics (`aulaquipu:doc`, `aulaquipu:graph`, …) and has `parallelToolCalls` on. A new `animationCreate` tool and an `aulaquipu:anim` topic follow the same pattern.
- The classroom page (`apps/web-app/app/aula/[sessionId]/page.tsx`) already has tabs for the document, graph and whiteboard.
- The machine had `ffmpeg` and Python 3.14 at the time of writing. It had no `manim` and no LaTeX.

## Design
1. **Two stages.** The realtime voice model must not write Manim code itself: it blocks speech and quality drops. `animationCreate({ title, concept })` returns immediately ("generating, keep talking"). A separate text-model call writes the scene from a strict template plus a short Manim skill prompt.
2. **Render.** Run `manim -ql` (480p, 15 fps) in a subprocess with a timeout. On an error, send the traceback back to the model and retry up to twice. A 5–10 s scene is roughly 10–30 s of render plus 5–15 s of code generation, so about 20–60 s end to end.
3. **Delivery.** Encode the mp4 as h264 yuv420p with faststart, upload to Supabase Storage, and publish a `ready` message with a signed URL on the data channel. Never send video over the channel (reliable messages are only a few KB). Also publish `pending` and `failed` states so the tab can show a spinner.
4. **Tell the agent.** When the job ends, inject a message into the running session (`session.generateReply` with instructions to comment on the animation). Not confirmed to work with the duplex realtime model: test this first. Don't interrupt the student mid-sentence.
5. **Persistence.** Log each animation in `session_events` so it survives a reload and shows up in the class summary.
6. **Tab UI.** List of animations with states: generating (spinner), ready (`<video controls loop muted>`), failed (short message). Show a dot on the tab when something becomes ready.

## Risks and mitigations
- **Running generated code (main risk).** This is a platform for minors and a student could prompt-inject the model.
  - Allowlist check on the code: only `from manim import *`; reject `os`, `subprocess`, `socket`, `open`, `eval`, `exec`, `__import__` and similar.
  - Sandbox: no network, non-root user, CPU, memory and time limits, read-only filesystem except a temp dir.
  - Limits: one job at a time per class and a daily cap per student. Moderate the request text too.
- **LaTeX.** `MathTex` and `Tex` need a LaTeX install (hundreds of MB). In v1, tell the template to use `Text`, shapes, axes and graphs only. Add minimal TeX Live (`texlive-latex-base`, fonts, `dvisvgm`) to the Docker image later.
- **Python and system dependencies.** Manim needs Cairo and Pango. Python 3.14 is probably too new for some dependencies (not checked): pin 3.11 or 3.12 in a `uv` venv. Add a setup script for local development and the system packages to the agent Dockerfile.
- **CPU and voice quality.** Rendering can starve the agent's realtime audio on the same machine. At minimum use `nice` and a thread limit; in production use a separate render worker or job queue.
- **Output quality.** LLM Manim code often overlaps objects, runs off screen or uses the wrong API version. Use a strict template with helpers (title, step reveal, axes plus function, labeled shapes), a few worked examples, a pinned Manim version and the retry loop.
- **Caching and fallbacks.** Cache by hash of (concept, level) so repeats are instant. Pre-render 5–8 secondary-school staples as instant fallbacks: function graph, fractions, Pythagoras, derivative tangent, probability. That also makes demos safe when generation fails.

## Effort estimate (MVP)
| Piece | Time |
| --- | --- |
| Python env, template and skill prompt | 3–4 h |
| Code generation, validation and retry loop | 3 h |
| Tool, async completion and agent notification | 2 h |
| Storage and the tab UI | 3 h |
| Sandbox and Docker | 3 h |

## Suggested first slice
Python env + template + render script + the tool and the tab, using pre-made scenes only. Add LLM code generation after that works end to end.

## Alternative or complement
Have the model output a small JSON scene spec (shapes, labels, steps) and render it in the browser with canvas or an animation library. It is instant and needs no Python. Manim stays as the "wow" path for richer scenes.
